goldStandard.objective: Show the useful work behind a CG Production House content run to earn qualified production and strategy enquiries in November.
goldStandard.audienceAndIntent: Business owners need to see how a brief becomes usable content and what to expect from a production partner.
goldStandard.coreMessage: A well-prepared shoot creates specific usable assets; demonstrate actual choices and permission-cleared outcomes.
goldStandard.formatsAndRationale: Build four linked production stories within four videos, eight photos and four posters. Each video explains one decision: brief, on-set framing, edit or review. Two supporting photographs per story show the real working detail and its approved result; one poster turns that decision into a practical client question. This makes the process tangible rather than repeating an agency promise. Use only permission-cleared material; examples are concepts, not booked shoots.
goldStandard.testAndChange: Compare process-led explanations with finished-work explanations on Facebook. Keep the service and observation age comparable, recording seven-day shares, substantive questions and attributable service enquiries. The selected September posts had 3–4 reactions, no comments and one recorded share on the shoot-planning example; that partial sample does not establish a winner. Note boosting and unequal exposure, and do not claim sales causation.
goldStandard.pillarsAndHooks: Planning one shoot; directing a scene; editing choices; client review; using approved content across channels.
goldStandard.mustAvoid: Do not expose client work, private files, staff identities, results or pricing without exact permission and current facts.
goldStandard.channelIntegration: Use verified CG Production House channels and the current website contact route; check consent for each example.
goldStandard.successSignals: For each story, record whether an enquiry names the service, business need, intended output and next step. Keep recorded discovery calls separate from confirmed projects. Use seven-day comments and shares as supporting attention signals only. Compare which explanation leads to a clearer brief; missing attribution or too few enquiries means the result is inconclusive.
goldStandard.nextMonthGamePlan: November sequence: first show the question that turns a vague request into a usable brief; next demonstrate one framing choice on set; then reveal an editing choice with its approved finished example; finally explain a client review checkpoint. Each story uses one video, two photos and one poster: four videos, eight photos and four posters overall. Set dates through the posting calendar after consent and production checks. Review equally aged responses at month end and carry the clearest service explanation into December, without a discount or guaranteed result.
